The Ministry of Education made an announcement today regarding a major expansion to Cuba’s University of Havana. In order to boost the number of skilled workers and revitalize interest in industry, the university will be expanding to include an engineering department. President Cortez praised the move, stating that Cubans needed to prepare themselves for a changing economy and an industrialized world.

La Facultad de Inginería will be built a kilometer south of the university’s main campus, which has been in operation since 1728. Set to be completed by the start of the school year in 2022, it will offer a small array of majors, including:

  • Mechanical engineering
  • Materials science
  • Aerospace engineering
  • Electrical engineering
  • Vehicle engineering

In addition to offering new study programs, the university has publicly announced a partnership with the Ciudad Libertad Airport in which they will encourage young men and women to earn their pilot’s license, which is an emergent profession amid positive growth in Cuba’s tourism industry.

Construction of the two-story concrete building is expected to cost the state just under $13.5 million USD, including the cost of furnishing the classrooms, setting up lab equipment necessary for the courses, and establishing a basic computer network for the faculty to utilize. No housing will be available directly on location, but students will be encouraged to reside in the main campus and commute to the engineering facility.
